rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book are Jews and Christians, whose disbelief is deviation concerning God's attributes; min is explanatory, and the polytheists are idol worshippers.
rows.anchor: اليهود والنصارى فإنهم كفروا بالإلحاد في صفات الله سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Munfakkin may mean that they would not abandon their religion, or that they would not abandon their pledge to follow the truth when the Messenger came.
rows.anchor: عما كانوا عليه من دينهم، أو الوعد باتباع الحق إذ جاءهم الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear proof may be the Messenger himself or the Quran, which makes the truth clear.
rows.anchor: الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام أو القرآن، فإنه مبين للحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear proof may be the Messenger's miraculous character and the Quran's silencing of anyone who challenges it.
rows.anchor: معجزة الرسول بأخلاقه والقرآن بإفحامه من تحدى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rasul min Allah may be an appositive to al-bayyina, directly or through an implied genitive, or it may begin a new nominal sentence.
rows.anchor: بنفسه أو بتقدير مضاف أو مبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although unlettered, the Prophet is like one reciting the scrolls because he recited what they contain.
rows.anchor: والرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام وإن كان أميا لكنه لما تلا مثل ما في الصحف كان كالتالي لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger reciting the scrolls may instead refer to Gabriel.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد جبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scrolls are purified because falsehood cannot reach their contents.
rows.anchor: أن الباطل لا يأتي ما فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scrolls are purified because only the purified touch them.
rows.anchor: أنها لا يمسها إلا المطهرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scrolls contain upright writings that speak the truth.
rows.anchor: مكتوبات مستقيمة ناطقة بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their division may mean that some left their former way by believing or becoming doubtful, or that they broke their pledge to persist in disbelief.
rows.anchor: عما كانوا عليه بأن آمن بعضهم أو تردد في دينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The division after proof parallels those who once sought victory over disbelievers but rejected what they recognized when it came.
rows.anchor: وكانوا من قبل يستفتحون على الذين كفروا فلما جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the People of the Book separately after grouping them with polytheists highlights how heinous their division was despite their knowledge, making others even more culpable by comparison.
rows.anchor: لما تفرقوا مع علمهم كان غيرهم بذلك أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their own scriptures commanded them to worship God alone, sincerely and without associating anything with Him.
rows.anchor: ليعبدوا الله مخلصين له الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hanifa means turning away from deviant beliefs.
rows.anchor: حنفاء } مائلين عن العقائد الزائغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were commanded to establish prayer and give zakat, but altered the prescriptions and disobeyed.
rows.anchor: ويؤتوا الزكوة } ولكنهم حرفوا وعصوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhalika din al-qayyima means the religion of the upright community.
rows.anchor: وذلك دين القيمة } دين الملة القيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their abiding in Hell may be on Judgment Day, or already apply by virtue of their deeds warranting it; shared punishment in kind does not entail identical types, which may vary with the two groups' disbelief.
rows.anchor: في الحال لملابستهم ما يوجب ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers are the worst of creation; Nafi reads al-bariyya with hamza, preserving its original form.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع «البريئة» بالهمز على الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who believe and do good are the best of creation.
rows.anchor: أولئك هم خير البرية جزاؤهم عند ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of the reward intensifies praise: reward signals recompense for their qualities, is from their Lord, and multiplies delight through plural gardens, their attribution and description, and emphasis on everlastingness.
rows.anchor: تقديم المدح، وذكر الجزاء المؤذن بأن ما منحوا في مقابلة ما وصفوا به والحكم عليه بأن من، { عند ربهم } ، وجمع { جنت } وتقييدها إضافة ووصفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's pleasure is an added gift beyond the reward, and they are pleased because it fulfills their ultimate wishes.
rows.anchor: رضى الله عنهم } استئناف بما يكون لهم زيادة على جزائهم. { ورضوا عنه } لأنه بلغهم أقصى أمانيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That refers to the reward and divine pleasure, promised to whoever fears the Lord, since fear is the basis of the matter and motive for every good.
rows.anchor: فإن الخشية ملاك الأمر والباعث على كل خير

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says that whoever recites this surah will be with the best of creation at the evening resting place on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
" من قرأ سورة لم يكن الذين كفروا كان يوم القيامة مع خير البرية مساء ومقيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earthquake is the disturbance appointed for the first or second blast, or the disturbance fitting the earth by its nature or by wisdom.
rows.anchor: المقدر لها عند النفخة الأولى، أو الثانية أو الممكن لها أو اللائق بها في الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with fatḥ on the zay makes zalzalah the name of the motion; faʿlal occurs only with doubled consonants.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالفتح وهو اسم الحركة وليس في الأبنية فعلال إلا في المضاعف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's burdens are either buried treasures or the dead; thiql means household goods.
rows.anchor: ما في جوفها من الدفائن أو الأموات جمع ثقل وهو متاع البيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People ask what is wrong with the earth because the event overwhelms them; another view takes al-insan to mean the disbeliever, since a believer knows what is happening.
rows.anchor: الكافر فإن المؤمن يعلم ما لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth may tell creatures its news through its state, or God may make it speak to report what was done upon it.
rows.anchor: وقيل ينطقها الله سبحانه وتعالى فتخبر بما عمل عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, yawm idhin may be appositional to idha, with both governed by tuhaddith; alternatively yawm idhin is an independent clause and idha is governed by an implied verb.
rows.anchor: أو أصل و { إذا } منتصب بمضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth reports because its Lord inspires it by causing events that signify its news, or by making it speak; the phrase may also explain its news, and the lām may mean to or retain its original sense of upon, since it takes satisfaction from sinners.
rows.anchor: بأن أحدث فيها ما دلت على الأخبار، أو أنطقها بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People depart from their exits from the graves toward the gathering place, scattered according to their ranks, to see the recompense for their deeds; a reading opens the yāʾ in yuraw.
rows.anchor: من مخارجهم من القبور إلى الموقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two descriptions of even the smallest good or evil deeds explain seeing the deeds; one reading vocalizes yarahu with ḍamma, and Hisham stills the hāʾ.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قرىء « يره» بالضم، وقرأ هشام بإسكان الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A disbeliever's good deed and a person who avoids major sins' evil deed may reduce their respective reward and punishment; alternatively the verses assume no annulment or forgiveness, or refer respectively to the blessed and wretched in light of their scattering.
rows.anchor: في نقص الثواب والعقاب. وقيل الآية مشروطة بعدم الإحباط والمغفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dharrat may mean a tiny ant or a mote of dust.
rows.anchor: وال { ذرة } النملة الصغيرة أو الهباء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises that reciting the surah four times is like reciting the whole Quran.
rows.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
" من قرأ سورة إذا زلزلت الأرض أربع مرات كان كمن قرأ القرآن كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rebukes and alerts rational people not to make worldly life their whole concern and greatest effort, because its outcome is loss and regret.
rows.anchor: ردع وتنبيه على أن العاقل ينبغي له أن لا يكون جميع همه ومعظم سعيه للدنيا فإن عاقبة ذلك وبال وحسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: You will learn your error when you witness what lies ahead; this warning is meant to make them fear and wake from heedlessness.
rows.anchor: خطأ رأيكم إذا عاينتم ما وراءكم وهو إنذار ليخافوا وينتبهوا من غفلتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repetition emphasizes the warning and thumma suggests that the second is stronger, or the first refers to death or the grave and the second to resurrection.
rows.anchor: تكرير للتأكيد وفي { ثم } دلالة على أن الثاني أبلغ من الأول، أو الأول عند الموت أو في القبر والثاني عند النشور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they knew what lay ahead with the certainty of what they already know, it would occupy them from other things; alternatively they would do what cannot be described or comprehended, with the answer omitted for emphasis.
rows.anchor: لشغلكم ذلك عن غيره، أو لفعلتم ما لا يوصف ولا يكتنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La-tarawunna al-jahim cannot answer the conditional because it is certain to happen; it instead answers an omitted oath, reinforcing the threat and clarifying the warning after its initial obscurity.
rows.anchor: لأنه محقق الوقوع بل هو جواب قسم محذوف أكد به الوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Amir and al-Kisai read the initial tāʾ of la-tarawunna with ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر والكسائي بضم التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated sight may emphasize the warning; the first may be seeing it from afar and the second upon reaching it, or the first may be knowledge and the second actual vision.
rows.anchor: تكرير للتأكيد، أو الأولى إذا رأيتهم من مكان بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ayn al-yaqin is vision that is itself certainty, since knowledge by direct observation is the highest degree of certainty.
rows.anchor: فإن علم المشاهدة أعلى مراتب اليقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing questioned is what distracted the addressees from religion; the address applies to anyone distracted by worldly life, and naim means the distracting things by contextual evidence and other texts.
rows.anchor: الذي ألهاكم، والخطاب مخصوص بكل من ألهاه دنياه عن دينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view makes the question universal because everyone is asked about gratitude for blessings; another restricts it to disbelievers.
rows.anchor: وقيل يعمان إذ كل يسأل عن شكره. وقيل الآية مخصوصة بالكفار

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says the reciter will not be reckoned for the worldly blessings God bestowed and receives the reward of reciting a thousand verses.
rows.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
" من قرأ ألهاكم لم يحاسبه الله سبحانه وتعالى بالنعيم الذي أنعم به عليه في دار الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rebukes the addressee's assumption; lanubadhanna means that he will be cast into the Hutama, a fire that crushes whatever is thrown into it.
rows.anchor: ردع له عن حسبانه. { لينبذن } ليطرحن. { فى الحطمة } في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma adraka asks about this fire with its special crushing property.
rows.anchor: النار التي لها هذه الخاصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nar Allah explains Hutama as a fire kindled by God, which no one else can extinguish.
rows.anchor: التي أوقدها الله وما أوقده لا يقدر غيره أن يطفئه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire rises to and surrounds the heart's center; the heart is singled out because it is the body's most delicate and painful part, or because it houses false beliefs and generates bad deeds.
rows.anchor: وتشتمل عليها، وتخصيصها بالذكر لأن الفؤاد ألطف ما في البدن وأشده ألما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muʾsada means shut or sealed, from the verb for closing a door; the cited verse witnesses this sense of the word.
rows.anchor:
مطبقة من أوصدت الباب إذا أطبقته، قال:
تحن إلى أجبال مكة ناقتي
ومن دونها أبواب صنعاء موصدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hafs, Abu Amr, and Hamza read the word with hamza.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حفص وأبو عمرو وحمزة بالهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are bound in extended columns like stocks used to restrain thieves; the Kufans except Hafs read umud with two dammas, and another reading stills the mīm with ḍamma on the ʿayn.
rows.anchor: مثل المقاطر التي تقطر فيها اللصوص وقرأ الكوفيون غير حفص بضمتين، وقرىء «عمد» بسكون الميم مع ضم العين

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises ten good deeds for each person who mocked Muhammad and his companions to whoever recites the surah.
rows.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
" من قرأ سورة الهمزة أعطاه الله عشر حسنات بعدد من استهزأ بمحمد عليه الصلاة والسلام وأصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to the Prophet, who did not witness the event but saw its traces and heard its reports by mass transmission, so it is as if he saw it.
rows.anchor: الخطاب للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم، وهو وإن لم يشهد تلك الوقعة لكن شاهد آثارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording how, rather than what, recalls signs of God's knowledge, power, honor for the House, and the Messenger's rank; the event was a prophetic precursor and reportedly occurred in his birth year.
rows.anchor: لأن المراد تذكير ما فيها من وجوه الدلالة على كمال علم الله تعالى وقدرته وعزة بيته وشرف رسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraha al-Ashram, Yemen's ruler under the Najashi, built the Qullays church in Sana'a to divert pilgrims; a man of Kinana defiled it at night, prompting Abraha to vow to destroy the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: أبرهة بن الصباح الأشرم ملك اليمن من قبل أصحمة النجاشي بنى كنيسة بصنعاء وسماها القليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraha marched with a strong elephant called Mahmud and other elephants; when directed toward the sanctuary it knelt and stopped, but ran when turned toward Yemen or elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وكان كلما وجهوه إلى الحرم برك ولم يبرح، وإذا رجعوه إلى اليمن أو إلى جهة أخرى هرول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent birds carrying stones in their beaks and on their feet, each stone larger than a lentil and smaller than a chickpea; it entered a man's head and exited behind, killing them all.
rows.anchor: أكبر من العدسة وأصغر من الحمصة، فترميهم فيقع الحجر في رأس الرجل فيخرج من دبره فهلكوا جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading alam tara strongly displays the effect of the jussive; kayfa is accusative as an object of the verb because it carries an interrogative sense.
rows.anchor: في إظهار أثر الجازم، وكيف نصب بفعل لأبتر لما فيه من معنى الاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their scheme aimed to disable and demolish the Kaaba; God rendered it futile by destroying them and magnifying the House's standing.
rows.anchor: في تعطيل الكعبة وتخريبها. { فى تضليل } في تضييع وإبطال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ababil are flocks, likened to a large bundle because the birds cluster together; alternatively, the word has no singular, like ababid and shamāṭiṭ.
rows.anchor: جماعات جمع إبالة وهي الحزمة الكبيرة، شبهت بها الجماعة من الطير في تضامها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yarmihim is also read with a masculine verb because tayr is a collective noun, or the verb may attach to the implied pronoun of Lord.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالياء على تذكير الطير لأنه اسم جمع، أو إسناده إلى ضمير ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sijjil may mean hardened clay from Persian sang-kil, derive from sijill meaning a large bucket, from isjal meaning sending, or mean a recorded portion of written punishment.
rows.anchor: من طين متحجر معرب سنككل وقيل من السجل وهو الدلو الكبير، أو الاسجال وهو الارسال، أو من السجل ومعناه من جملة العذاب المكتوب المدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eaten straw may be leaves consumed by worms, husks left after their grain was eaten, or straw chewed and excreted by animals.
rows.anchor: كورق زرع وقع فيه، والآكال وهو أن يأكله الدود أو أكل حبه فبقي صفرا منه، أو كتين أكلته الدواب وراثته

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises protection from sinking into the earth and transformation during life to whoever recites the surah.
rows.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
" من قرأ سورة الفيل أعفاه الله أيام حياته من الخسف والمسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilaf Quraysh attaches to let them worship the Lord of this House; the fa implies a condition: if they will not worship for God's countless other favors, they should worship for their trading journeys.
rows.anchor: والفاء لما في الكلام من معنى الشرط، إذ المعنى أن نعم الله عليهم لا تحصى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their winter journey went to Yemen and their summer journey to Syria, where they obtained provisions and traded.
rows.anchor: أي الرحلة في الشتاء إلى اليمن وفي الصيف إلى الشام فيمتارون ويتجرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively the phrase may depend on an implied verb of wonder or on the preceding surah by poetic incorporation; Ubayy's codex supports treating the two as one surah.
rows.anchor: أو بما قبله كالتضمين في الشعر أي { فجعلهم كعصف مأكول } { لإيلف قريش } ، ويؤيده أنهما في مصحف أبي سورة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading says liyaʾlaf Quraysh ilafahum rihlah; Quraysh descends from al-Nadr ibn Kinana, and the name derives from the qirsh sea creature that dominates and consumes without being consumed; its diminutive form magnifies it.
rows.anchor: وهو دابة عظيمة في البحر تعبث بالسفن فلا تطاق إلا بالنار، فشبهوا بها لأنها تأكل ولا تؤكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name is unqualified first and then restricted by an apposition for emphasis; Ibn Amir reads liʾlaf without a yāʾ after the hamza.
rows.anchor: وصغر الاسم للتعظيم وإطلاق الإيلاف، ثم إبدال المقيد عنه للتفخيم. وقرأ ابن عامر «لئلاف» بغير ياء بعد الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God fed Quraysh from hunger through the two journeys, with the indefinite form magnifying the blessing; another view refers to a severe famine when they ate carrion and bones.
rows.anchor: أي بالرحلتين والتنكير للتعظيم، وقيل المراد به شدة أكلوا فيها الجيف والعظام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God secured them from the People of the Elephant, from being snatched in their homeland or travels, or from leprosy in their own country.
rows.anchor: أصحاب الفيل أو التخطف في بلدهم ومسايرهم، أو الجذام فلا يصيبهم ببلدهم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises ten good deeds for each person who circumambulates or worshipfully stays at the Kaaba to the reciter of this surah.
rows.anchor:
عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
" من قرأ سورة لإيلاف قريش أعطاه الله عشر حسنات بعدد من طاف بالكعبة واعتكف بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Araʾayta is an interrogative of astonishment; it is read arayta without hamza by analogy with the imperfect, and the initial interrogative may ease its form; araʾaytaka adds the kāf.
rows.anchor: عناه التعجب، وقرىء «أريت» بلا همز إلحاقا بالمضارع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-din may mean requital or Islam, and the relative expression may be generic or refer to a known person; the following verse supports the latter.
rows.anchor: بالجزاء أو الإسلام والذي يحتمل الجنس والعهد ويؤيد الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who violently shoves the orphan may be Abu Jahl, who pushed away an orphan under his guardianship seeking his own property; or Abu Sufyan, who beat a child seeking meat after slaughtering a camel; or al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, or a miserly hypocrite.
rows.anchor: وهو أبو جهل كان وصيا ليتيم فجاءه عريانا يسأله من مال نفسه فدفعه، أو أبو سفيان نحر جزورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yadaʿ is also read to mean that he leaves the orphan alone.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «يدع» أي يترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He neither urges his family nor anyone else to feed the poor; because he does not believe in requital, this clause follows the denial with fa.
rows.anchor: على طعام المسكين } لعدم اعتقاده بالجزاء ولذلك رتب الجملة على { يكذب } بالفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Woe is for worshippers who are inattentive to their prayers, heedless and unconcerned about them.
rows.anchor: ساهون } أي غافلون غير مبالين بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aʿṭaynaka is also read anṭaynaka; al-kawthar is abundant good, including knowledge, deeds, and honor in both abodes.
rows.anchor: قرىء «أنطيناك». { الكوثر } الخير المفرط الكثرة من العلم والعمل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet identifies al-kawthar as a river in Paradise promised by God, rich in good, sweeter than honey, whiter than milk, colder than snow, softer than butter, with emerald banks and silver vessels, whose drinker never thirsts.
rows.anchor: روي عنه عليه الصلاة والسلام أنه نهر في الجنة وعدنيه ربي فيه خير كثير أحلى من العسل وأبيض من اللبن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations identify al-kawthar as a pool in Paradise, the Prophet's children and followers, the scholars of his community, or the great Quran.
rows.anchor: وقيل حوض فيها وقيل أولاده وأتباعه، أو علماء أمته والقرآن العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is to be continued sincerely for God, in contrast with inattentive or ostentatious worship, as thanks for His favor because prayer gathers all forms of gratitude.
rows.anchor: شكرا لإنعامه، فإن الصلاة جامعة لأقسام الشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wanhar commands sacrificing choice camels, the Arabs' finest property, and giving to the needy, in contrast with refusing the orphan and withholding aid.
rows.anchor: البدن التي هي خيار أموال العرب وتصدق على المحاويج خلافا لمن يدعهم ويمنع عنهم الماعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer may specifically mean the Eid prayer and sacrifice the offering of an animal.
rows.anchor: وقد فسرت الصلاة بصلاة العيد والنحر بالتضحية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who hates the Prophet is a hater because God hates him.
rows.anchor: إن من أبغضك لبغضه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's hater is cut off without descendants or good remembrance, while the Prophet's descendants, renown, virtues, and immeasurable afterlife reward endure.
rows.anchor: ولا حسن ذكر، وأما أنت فتبقى ذريتك وحسن صيتك وآثار فضلك إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises that the reciter will drink from every river in Paradise and receive ten good deeds for each sacrifice offered by worshippers on the great day of sacrifice.
rows.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
" من قرأ سورة الكوثر سقاه الله من كل نهر له في الجنة، ويكتب له عشر حسنات بعدد كل قربان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address targets particular disbelievers whom God knew would never believe.
rows.anchor: يعني كفرة مخصوصين قد علم الله منهم أنهم لا يؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A group of Quraysh offered that Muhammad worship their gods for one year and they worship his God for one year, whereupon the surah was revealed.
rows.anchor: روي أن رهطا من قريش قالوا يا محمد تعبد آلهتنا سنة ونعبد إلهك سنة فنزلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La aʿbudu refers to the future; an enters only an imperfect with future sense, whereas ma enters an imperfect with present sense.
rows.anchor: فأن لا تدخل إلا على مضارع بمعنى الاستقبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressees' not worshipping what the Prophet worships is future because it is paired with la aʿbudu.
rows.anchor: لأنه في قران { لا أعبد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's not worshipping what they worshipped refers to the present or the past.
rows.anchor: أي في الحال أو فيما سلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated clause may mean that they never worship at any time what the Prophet worships; alternatively both repeated clauses emphasize the preceding statement in a stronger form.
rows.anchor: أي وما عبدتم في وقت ما أنا عابده، ويجوز أن يكونا تأكيدين على طريقة أبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording ma ʿabadtum rather than ma ʿabadt is used because they were identified with idolatry before the mission, whereas the Prophet was not then identified with worship of God.
rows.anchor: وأما لم يقل ما عبدت ليطابق { ما عبدتم } لأنهم كانوا موسومين قبل المبعث بعبادة الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma rather than man may refer to attributes, meaning falsehood versus truth, or be used for agreement; alternatively it may be a verbal noun, with the first two relative pronouns and the last two verbal nouns.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال { ما } دون من لأن المراد الصفة كأنه قال: لا أعبد الباطل ولا تعبدون الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressees retain their religion, and the Prophet retains his; this neither permits disbelief nor forbids fighting so as to be abrogated by the fighting verse, unless it means leaving each group to its religion.
rows.anchor: الذي أنتم عليه لا تتركونه. { ولى دين } ديني الذي أنا عليه لا أرفضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Din has also been interpreted as accounting and requital, supplication, or worship.
rows.anchor: وقد فسر ال { دين } بالحساب والجزاء والدعاء والعبادة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says its reciter is as if reciting a quarter of the Quran, is distanced from rebellious devils, and is free of polytheism.
rows.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
" من قرأ سورة الكافرون فكأنما قرأ ربع القرآن وتباعدت عنه مردة الشياطين وبرىء من الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's aid is His victory for the Prophet over his enemies; the conquest is Mecca, or the phrase means God's general victory and conquest of Mecca and other lands for believers.
rows.anchor: إظهاره إياك على أعدائك. { والفتح } وفتح مكة، وقيل المراد جنس نصر الله المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Describing victory as coming suggests that decreed events approach their appointed times gradually; since victory is near, the Prophet should await it and prepare to thank God.
rows.anchor: وإنما عبر عن الحصول بالمجيء تجوزا للإشعار بأن المقدرات متوجهة من الأزل إلى أوقاتها المعينة لها فتقرب منها شيئا فشيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People enter God's religion in dense groups, including Meccans, people of Taif and Yemen, Hawazin, and other Arab tribes.
rows.anchor: جماعات كثيفة كأهل مكة والطائف واليمن وهوازن وسائر قبائل العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yadkhulun is a circumstantial clause if raʾayta means seeing, or a second object if it means knowing.
rows.anchor: حال على أن { رأيت } بمعنى أبصرت أو مفعول ثان على أنه بمعنى علمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih with praise may express wonder at God's enabling what no one imagined, prayerful praise for His blessings, declaring Him above what wrongdoers said while affirming His promise, or extolling majesty while praising generosity.
rows.anchor: فتعجب لتيسير الله ما لم يخطر ببال أحد حامدا له، أو فصل له حامدا على نعمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet entered Mecca, began at the mosque, entered the Kaaba, and prayed eight rakʿas.
rows.anchor: روي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم لما دخل مكة بدأ بالمسجد فدخل الكعبة وصلى ثمان ركعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking forgiveness humbles oneself, treats one's own deeds as insufficient, and compensates for turning attention toward anything besides God; it may instead be asking forgiveness for the community.
rows.anchor: وقيل استغفره لأمتك، وتقديم التسبيح على الحمد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet reported seeking God's forgiveness one hundred times by day and night.
rows.anchor:
وعنه عليه الصلاة والسلام
" إني لأستغفر الله في اليوم والليلة مائة مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order moves downward from the Creator to creation: glorification, praise, then asking forgiveness, as in the saying that one sees God before seeing anything.
rows.anchor: وتقديم التسبيح على الحمد ثم الحمد على الاستغفار على طريق النزول من الخالق إلى الخلق. كما قيل ما رأيت شيئا إلا ورأيت الله قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has always been the One who turns toward whoever seeks His forgiveness, from the time He created accountable beings.
rows.anchor: لمن استغفره مذ خلق المكلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most hold that the surah preceded the conquest and foretold the Prophet's death: al-Abbas wept, saying it announced his death, and the Prophet agreed; it signaled completion of the mission and religion like 5:3, or nearness of death through the command to seek forgiveness, so it is called the Farewell surah.
rows.anchor: والأكثر على أن السورة نزلت قبل فتح مكة، وأنه نعي لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises the reward of one who witnessed the conquest of Mecca alongside Muhammad to whoever recites this surah.
rows.anchor:
وعنه عليه الصلاة والسلام
" من قرأ سورة إذا جاء أعطي من الأجر كمن شهد مع محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام يوم فتح مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabbat means perished or lost; tabab is loss leading to destruction.
rows.anchor: هلكت أو خسرت والتباب خسران يؤدي إلى الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two hands mean Abu Lahab himself, as in 2:195; alternatively they refer to this world and the next.
rows.anchor: ولا تلقوا بأيديكم إلى التهلكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When 26:214 was revealed, Abu Lahab objected and picked up a stone to throw at Muhammad, and this surah then came down.
rows.anchor: جمع أقاربه فأنذرهم فقال أبو لهب: تبا لك ألهذا دعوتنا، وأخذ حجرا ليرميه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is called Abu Lahab because the honorific was familiar, his personal name Abd al-Uzza was disliked, the epithet better suits a person of the Fire, or it echoes the phrase fire of flame.
rows.anchor: ولأن اسمه عبد العزى فاستكره ذكره، ولأنه لما كان من أصحاب النار كانت الكنية أوفق بحاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading Abu Lahab in the nominative is like saying Ali ibn Abu Talib.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «أبو لهب» كما قيل علي بن أبو طالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa tabb reports after the curse, using the past for a certain future as supported by a poetic line and a reading wa qad tabb; alternatively the first reports what his hands did and the second his own deeds.
rows.anchor: ويدل عليه أنه قرىء «وقد تب» أو الأول إخبار عما كسبت يداه والثاني عن عمل نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma aghna negates that his wealth helped when destruction arrived, or is a rhetorical question denying that it helped.
rows.anchor: نفي لإغناء المال عنه حين نزل به التباب أو استفهام إنكار له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What he acquired may be profits, status and followers gained through wealth, what he thought his deeds would earn him, or his son Utbah, who a lion attacked on the road to Syria.
rows.anchor: من النتائج والأرباح والوجاهة والإتباع، أو عمله الذي ظن أنه ينفعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Lahab died from smallpox a few days after Badr; his body was left until it decomposed and enslaved Black men were hired to bury it, fulfilling the unseen report.
rows.anchor: ومات أبو لهب بالعدسة بعد وقعة بدر بأيام معدودة، وترك ثلاثا حتى أنتن ثم استأجروا بعض السودان حتى دفنوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He will enter a blazing fire, meaning Hell; the wording does not prove he never believes because burning could be for wickedness.
rows.anchor: اشتعال يريد نار جهنم، وليس فيه ما يدل على أنه لا يؤمن لجواز أن يكون صليها للفسق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sayasla is read with a lightened form and ḍamma, or with doubling.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { سيصلى } بالضم مخففا و { سيصلى } مشددا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His wife is either coordinated with the implied subject of sayasla or made the subject of a new sentence; she is Umm Jamil, Abu Sufyan's sister.
rows.anchor: عطف على المستتر في { سيصلى } أو مبتدأ وهي أم جميل أخت أبي سفيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hammalat al-hatab may mean carrying Hell's firewood, namely the sins of opposing the Messenger and urging her husband to harm him; a fire of discord; or bundles of thorn and brush she scattered in his path at night.
rows.anchor: يعني حطب جهنم فإنها كانت تحمل الأوزار بمعاداة الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم وتحمل زوجها على إيذائه، أو اليميمة فإنها كانت توقد نار الخصومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asim reads hammalata in the accusative as an insult.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم بالنصب على الشتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masad is something twisted together; mamsud describes a well-knit body, and the image either extends the metaphor or depicts her carrying a bundle tied at her neck in humiliation.
rows.anchor: ومنه رجل ممسود الخلق أي مجدوله، وهو ترشيح للمجاز أو تصوير لها بصورة الخطابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively it depicts her punishment in Hell, carrying a bundle such as zaqqum or darīʿ, with a fiery chain at her neck.
rows.anchor: حزمة من حطب جهنم كالزقوم، والضريع وفي جيدها سلسلة من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepositional phrase may be circumstantial or predicate, with habl raised by it.
rows.anchor: والظرف في موضع الحال أو الخبر وحبل مرتفع به

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet hoped that the reader of Tabbat would not be gathered with Abu Lahab in one abode.
rows.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
" من قرأ سورة تبت رجوت أن لا يجمع الله بينه وبين أبي لهب في دار واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun huwa may refer to the matter itself, serving as subject with the following sentence as predicate and needing no resumptive pronoun; or it answers the question about God, with ahad as apposition or a second predicate.
rows.anchor: الضمير للشأن كقولك: هو زيد منطلق وارتفاعه بالابتداء وخبره الجملة ولا حاجة إلى العائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh asked Muhammad to describe the Lord to whom he called them, and the surah was revealed; in that reading, God is what they asked about.
rows.anchor: روي أن قريشا قالوا: يا محمد صف لنا ربك الذي تدعونا إليه فنزلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahad gathers the attributes of majesty: true oneness excludes composition, multiplicity, embodiment, location, shared essence and its properties, while implying necessary existence, innate power, perfect wisdom and divinity.
rows.anchor: واحد بدل أو خبر ثان يدل على مجامع صفات الجلال كما دل الله على جميع صفات الكمال إذا الواحد الحقيقي ما يكون منزه الذات عن أنحاء التركيب والتعدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading huwa Allah omits qul; qul is necessary in al-Kafirun but unsuitable in Tabbat, since those surahs oppose or leave the Prophet's uncle, whereas here he declares monotheism and is also commanded to proclaim it.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «هو الله» بلا { قل } مع الاتفاق على أنه لا بد منه في { قل يا أيها الكفرون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Samad is the master toward whom needs are directed; He is absolutely independent, while all else depends on Him in every respect.
rows.anchor: السيد المصمود إليه في الحوائج من صمد إليه إذا قصد، وهو الموصوف به على الإطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite form reflects their knowledge of God's being Samad, unlike His oneness; repeating Allah signals that only one with these traits deserves deity, and the clause lacks a conjunction because it is a result or proof of the first.
rows.anchor: وتعريفه لعلمهم بصمديته بخلاف أحديته وتكرير لفظة { الله } للإشعار بأن من لم يتصف به لم يستحق الألوهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He does not beget because He has no likeness, need of a helper, successor, or susceptibility to need or extinction; past tense may answer claims that angels are God's daughters or the Messiah His son, or match the next clause.
rows.anchor: ولعل الاقتصاد على لفظ الماضي لوروده ردا على من قال الملائكة بنات الله، أو المسيح ابن الله أو ليطابق قوله: { ولم يولد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He was not begotten because He does not need anything and was not preceded by nonexistence.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأنه لا يفتقر إلى شيء ولا يسبقه عدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No mate or other being matches or resembles Him; the prepositional phrase is fronted from its expected position after kufuwan to emphasize denying equality with His essence.
rows.anchor: أي ولم يكن أحد يكافئه أو يماثله من صاحبة أو غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively the phrase is a circumstantial complement of the hidden subject in kufuwan, or a predicate, while kufuwan is circumstantial to ahad.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون حالا من المستكن في { كفوا } أو خبرا، ويكون { كفوا } حالا من { أحد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three clauses are linked because they deny all categories of likeness together as one thought.
rows.anchor: ولعل ربط الجمل الثلاث بالعطف لأن المراد منها نفي أقسام المكافأة فهي كجملة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza, Yaqub, and one transmission of Nafi read kufu with a light form; Hafs uses a vocalized form and changes hamza to waw.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة ويعقوب ونافع في رواية «كفوا» بالتخفيف، وحفص { كفوا } بالحركة وقلب الهمزة واوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brief surah contains all divine teachings and rejects doctrinal deviations; it equals a third of the Quran because the Quran's purposes are creed, rulings, and stories, and only the primary purpose is considered in equivalence to the whole.
rows.anchor: جاء في الحديث أنها تعدل ثلث القرآن

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet heard a man reciting the surah and said that Paradise had become due to him.
rows.anchor:
وعنه صلى الله عليه وسلم،
" أنه سمع رجلا يقرؤها فقال: «وجبت»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-falaq is what is split open, a verbal form meaning the passive; it broadly covers all possible things, since God split nonexistence's darkness with the light of creation, especially springs, rain, plants, and children emerging from an origin.
rows.anchor: ما يفلق عنه أي يفرق كالفرق فعل بمعنى مفعول، وهو يعم جميع الممكنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In common usage al-falaq means dawn; it suits the refuge because dawn changes the night from fear to the joy of light, resembles the start of Judgment Day, and shows that the One who removes night can remove what the supplicant fears.
rows.anchor: ويختص عرفا بالصبح ولذلك فسر به. وتخصيصه لما فيه من تغير الحال وتبدل وحشة الليل بسرور النور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name Lord is especially apt here because seeking refuge concerns warding off harms.
rows.anchor: ولفظ الرب هنا أوقع من سائر أسمائه تعالى لأن الإعاذة من المضار قريبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking refuge from the evil of what He created singles out the created realm because the realm of command is wholly good; evil in creation is voluntary, including disbelief and injustice, or natural, such as fire burning and poisons killing.
rows.anchor: خص عالم الخلق بالاستعاذة عنه لانحصار الشرفية، فإن عالم الأمر خير كله، وشره اختياري لازم ومتعد كالكفر والظلم، وطبيعي كإحراق النار وإهلاك السموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghasiq may be a very dark night, from the word for fullness as when an eye fills with tears, or from flowing, as darkness pours in or tears flow; night is specified because harms multiply and are harder to prevent, as the saying goes that night hides harm.
rows.anchor: ليل عظيم ظلامه من قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively ghasiq is the moon, which darkens during an eclipse, and its entry is entry into eclipse.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد به القمر فإنه يكسف فيغسق ووقوبه دخوله في الكسوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naffathat refers to souls or sorcerous women who tie knots in threads and blow on them; nafth is blowing with saliva.
rows.anchor: ومن شر النفوس أو النساء السواحر اللاتي يعقدن عقدا في خيوط وينفثن عليها، والنفث النفخ مع ريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says a Jewish man bewitched the Prophet with eleven knots on a bowstring hidden in a well; the Prophet became ill, the two refuge surahs were revealed, Gabriel showed its location, Ali retrieved it, and recitation untied one knot at a time and brought relief.
rows.anchor: لما روي أن يهوديا سحر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في إحدى عشرة عقدة في وتر دسه في بئر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This does not affirm the disbelievers' claim that he was bewitched, since they meant that magic had made him insane.
rows.anchor: ولا يوجب ذلك صدق الكفرة في أنه مسحور، لأنهم أرادوا به أنه مجنون بواسطة السحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, blowing on knots means undoing men's resolve through trickery, metaphorically like loosening knots by saliva; the definite article singles out every wicked female blower, unlike every night-darkness or envier.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالنفث في العقد إبطال عزائم الرجال بالحيل مستعار من تليين العقد بنفث الريق ليسهل حلها وإفرادها بالتعريف لأن كل نفاثة شريرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An envier harms when displaying envy and acting on it; before that he only grieves at the envied person's happiness, and envy is singled out as a chief source of harm one person or animal causes another.
rows.anchor: إذا أظهر حسده وعمل بمقتضاه، فإنه لا يعود ضرر منه قبل ذلك إلى المحسود بل يخص به لاغتمامه بسروره، وتخصيصه لأنه العمدة في إضرار الإنسان بل الحيوان غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In an allegorical reading, ghasiq means darkness or something without light, such as faculties.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بالغاسق ما يخلو عن النور وما يضاهيه كالقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In an allegorical reading, naffathat are plants whose vegetative powers expand their length, width, and depth as if blowing into three knots.
rows.anchor: النفثت } النباتات، فإن قواها النباتية من حيث أنها تزيد في طولها وعرضها وعمقها كانت تنفث في العقد الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In an allegorical reading, the envier is an animal, which often targets another out of desire for what it possesses; these three are singled out as proximate causes of harm.
rows.anchor: وبالحاسد الحيوان فإنه إنما يقصد غيره غالبا طمعا فيما عنده، ولعل إفرادها من عالم الخلق لأنها الأسباب القريبة للمضرة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that two surahs were revealed to him like no others, and that no two surahs are more beloved and pleasing to God than the two refuges.
rows.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
" لقد أنزلت علي سورتان ما أنزل مثلهما وإنك لن تقرأ سورتين أحب ولا أرضى عند الله منهما يعني المعوذتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In both refuge surahs a reading drops the hamza and transfers its vowel to the lām.
rows.anchor: وقرىء في السورتين بحذف الهمزة ونقل حركتهما إلى اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding surah seeks refuge from bodily harms common to humans and other beings; this surah concerns harms to human souls, so the addition is generalized and then specified to people, seeking refuge from the whisperer with their Lord who controls them and deserves their worship.
rows.anchor: عمم الإضافة ثم وخصصها بالناس ها هنا فكأنه قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Malik al-nas and ilah al-nas explain Lord: a lord need not be king, nor a king God; the order shows God's worthiness and power to grant refuge and stages knowing Him from blessings, to absolute sovereignty, to exclusive right to worship.
rows.anchor: عطفا بيان له فإن الرب قد لا يكون ملكا والملك قد لا يكون إلها، وفي هذا النظم دلالة على أنه حقيق بالإعاذة قادرا عليها غير ممنوع عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The progression in seeking refuge follows the progression of knowledge, treats different attributes as different essences to signal the danger, and repeats al-nas for clarification and to honor humanity.
rows.anchor: ويتدرج وجوه الاستعاذة كما يتدرج في الاستعاذة المعتادة، تنزيلا لاختلاف الصفات منزلة اختلاف الذات إشعارا بعظم الآفة المستعاذة منها، وتكرير { الناس } لما في الإظهار من مزيد البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-waswas is whispering, analogous to zalzal meaning shaking; with kasra it is the verbal noun, while here it means the whisperer named for his action as an intensification.
rows.anchor: أي الوسوسة كالزلزال بمعنى الزلزلة، وأما المصدر فبالكسر كالزلزال، والمراد به الموسوس وسمي بفعله مبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-khannas is one who habitually withdraws when a person remembers his Lord.
rows.anchor: الذي عادته أن يخنس أي يتأخر إذا ذكر الإنسان ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whisperer whispers in people's breasts when they neglect remembering God, like the imaginative faculty, which helps reason with premises but withdraws near the conclusion and plants doubt.
rows.anchor: إذا غفلوا عن ذكر ربهم، وذلك كالقوة الوهمية، فإنها تساعد العقل في المقدمات، فإذا آل الأمر إلى النتيجة خنست وأخذت توسوسه وتشككه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ladhi may be genitive as an adjective, or accusative or nominative as a censure.
rows.anchor: ومحل { الذي } الجر على الصفة أو النصب أو الرفع على الذم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min al-jinnati wa al-nas may explain the whisperer, al-ladhi, or attach to yuwaswisu, meaning that whispering comes from jinn and people; another view explains al-nas as encompassing both kinds, strained unless it means those who forget God's due, as in 54:6.
rows.anchor: بيان ل { الوسواس } ، أو الذي أو متعلق ب { يوسوس } أي يوسوس في صدورهم من جهة الجنة والناس. وقيل بيان ل { الناس }

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says reciting the two refuge surahs is like reciting the books God sent down.
rows.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
" من قرأ المعوذتين فكأنما قرأ الكتب التي أنزلها الله تبارك وتعالى
